passages.text: The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto. We prepared our consolidated financial statements in accordance with GAAP. Additional sections in this report which should be helpful to the reading of our discussion and analysis include the following: (i) a description of our business strategy found in Items 1 and 2. “ Business and Properties—Narrative Description of Business—Business Strategy; ” (ii) a description of developments during 2025, found in Items 1 and 2. “ Business and Properties—General Development of Business—Recent Developments; ” (iii) a description of terms for services and commodities we provide, found in Items 1 and 2. “Business and Properties—Narrative Description of Business—Business Segments;” (iv) a description of risk factors affecting us and our business, found in Item 1A. “ Risk Factors; ” and (v) a discussion of forward-looking statements, found in “ Information Regarding Forward-Looking Statements ” at the beginning of this report. A comparative discussion of our 2024 to 2023 operating results can be found in Item 7. “ Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Results of Operations ” included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 filed with the SEC on February 13, 2025. Critical Accounting Estimates Critical accounting estimates and assumptions involve material levels of subjectivity and complex judgment to account for highly uncertain matters or matters with a high susceptibility to change, and could result in a material impact to our financial statements. Examples of certain areas that require more judgment relative to others when preparing our consolidated financial statements and related disclosures include our use of estimates in determining (i) revenue recognition; (ii) income taxes; (iii) the economic useful lives of our assets and related depreciation and depletion rates; (iv) the fair values used in (a) assignment of the purchase price for a business acquisition, (b) calculations of possible asset and equity investment impairment charges, (c) calculation for the annual goodwill impairment test (or interim tests if triggered), and (d) recording derivative contract assets and liabilities; (v) reserves for environmental claims, legal fees, transportation rate cases, and other litigation liabilities; (vi) provisions for credit losses; and (vii) exposures under contractual indemnifications. We routinely evaluate these estimates, utilizing historical experience, consultation with experts and other methods we consider reasonable in the particular circumstances. Nevertheless, actual results may differ significantly from our estimates, and any effects on our business, financial position or results of operations resulting from revisions to these estimates are recorded in the period in which the facts that give rise to the revision become known. For a summary of our significant accounting policies, see Note 2 “Summary of Significant Accounting Policies” to our consolidated financial statements and the following discussion for further information regarding critical accounting estimates and assumptions used in the preparation of our financial statements. For discussion on our hedging activities and related sensitivities to our estimates, see Note 13 “Risk Management” to our consolidated financial statements and Item 7A. “ Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk ,” respectively. Impairments In addition to our annual goodwill impairment testing, we evaluate our goodwill, long-lived assets, and equity method investments for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that their carrying amounts may not be recoverable. Management applies judgment in assessing whether such triggering events have occurred. Impairment testing requires estimating fair value, which involves the use of significant estimates and assumptions regarding the timing and amounts of future cash inflows and outflows, commodity prices, discount rates, market multiples, and asset lives, among other items and as applicable. These estimates can be affected by a variety of factors, including external factors such as industry and macroeconomic conditions, and internal factors such as changes in our business strategy and our internal forecasts. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin sits above the sector median, reflecting fee-based natural gas transmission and midstream economics rather than commodity-exposed earnings; the margin eased modestly year over year but remains a durable competitive advantage for this issuer.

Operating cash flow covers capital spending plus dividends, and free cash flow covers shareholder distributions, so internal generation funds the equity return without incremental borrowing; buybacks are absent, leaving the distribution burden modest relative to cash generation.

key_risks.text: Gross and net leverage sit below the sector median and eased year over year, yet the indicative financial risk profile remains aggressive and headroom to the next leverage band boundary is thin, so a modest EBITDA decline or debt-funded acquisition would pressure the profile.

Impairment testing relies on judgment over commodity prices, discount rates and asset lives; revisions to those estimates could produce material charges against a large midstream asset base, weakening reported earnings and covenant-relevant EBITDA.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage improved year over year and sits marginally above the sector median, but EBITDA coverage trails the sector median, indicating the debt stack is large relative to earnings; cash interest paid is used as the interest proxy, so coverage is a cash-basis measure.

The maturity ladder is well spread, with the bulk of principal due after year five and only a modest slice falling in the next twelve months; near-term refinancing needs are manageable against operating cash flow and the undrawn credit facility and commercial paper program.

overall_credit_view.text: Leverage below the sector median and improving coverage support an investment-grade-style profile, but the indicative aggressive risk band and thin headroom to the next threshold mean the issuer has limited capacity for debt-funded expansion or EBITDA erosion before the profile weakens.

Cash flow conversion is solid and free cash flow covers dividends, but a low current ratio and heavy long-dated debt mean liquidity depends on continued market access; our forward view is stable leverage with distributions absorbing most free cash flow, absent large acquisitions.

credit_strengths.text: 營運利潤率處於行業中位數之上，反映以收費為基礎的天然氣輸送及中游經濟效益，而非受商品價格影響的盈利；利潤率按年溫和放緩，但對該發行人而言仍屬持久的競爭優勢。
營運現金流足以覆蓋資本開支加股息，自由現金流足以覆蓋股東分派，因此內部產生的資金可在不增加借貸的情況下支持股權回報；並無回購，令分派負擔相對於現金產生而言屬溫和。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿及淨槓桿處於行業中位數之下並按年放緩，但指示性財務風險狀況仍屬進取，且距離下一槓桿區間界限的緩衝空間狹窄，因此EBITDA溫和下降或債務融資收購將對該狀況構成壓力。
減值測試依賴對商品價格、折現率及資產可使用年限的判斷；該等估計的修訂可能對龐大的中游資產基礎產生重大減值費用，削弱報告盈利及與契約相關的EBITDA。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按年改善並略高於行業中位數，但EBITDA覆蓋率落後於行業中位數，顯示債務規模相對於盈利而言龐大；已付現金利息用作利息代理，因此覆蓋率屬現金基礎的衡量指標。
到期結構分佈良好，大部分本金於五年後到期，僅少量於未來十二個月內到期；相對於營運現金流及未提取的信貸融資和商業票據計劃，近期再融資需求屬可控。

overall_credit_view.text: 槓桿低於行業中位數及覆蓋率改善支持投資級別式的狀況，但指示性進取風險區間及距離下一門檻的狹窄緩衝空間，意味該發行人在狀況轉弱前，對債務融資擴張或EBITDA侵蝕的承受能力有限。
現金流轉換穩健且自由現金流覆蓋股息，但流動比率偏低及大量長年期債務意味流動性依賴持續的市場准入；我們的前瞻觀點為槓桿穩定，分派吸收大部分自由現金流，前提是並無大型收購。
